extracted.intended_audience: general readers, online community moderators, researchers, and journalists interested in online deception and moderation
extracted.subtask_description: Summarize and evaluate what sock puppet accounts are, why they are created, how they are used, how they are detected, and the legal/community consequences. Useful for moderators, researchers, and journalists studying online deception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of a sock puppet account
rubrics_metrics.description: A sock puppet, sock puppet account, or simply sock is a false online identity used for deceptive purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page notes the term originally referred to a hand puppet made from a sock and that online sockpuppets are used for disguised activity by the operator. This is the canonical definitional criterion for classifying an account as a sockpuppet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purposes for creating sockpuppets
rubrics_metrics.description: Sock puppets include online identities created to praise, defend, or support a person or organization, to manipulate public opinion, or to circumvent restrictions such as viewing a social media account that a user is blocked from.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this list of motivations when evaluating whether pseudonymous accounts are benign pseudonymity or deceptive sockpuppetry. Presence of one or more of these goals is indicative of deceptive intent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Block evasion (type)
rubrics_metrics.description: One reason for sockpuppeting is to circumvent a block, ban, or other form of sanction imposed on the person's original account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Platform moderators should treat accounts that appear to exist primarily to avoid sanctions as block-evasion sockpuppets and consult block-evasion policies (e.g., Wikipedia:Block evasion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ballot stuffing / Sybil-type manipulation (type)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sockpuppets may be created during an online poll to increase the puppeteer's votes or to create multiple identities each supporting the puppeteer's views, attempting to position the puppeteer as representing majority opinion and sideline opposition voices (a Sybil attack).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes stealth marketing, fake-support campaigns, and review-bombing on aggregator sites; evaluate for coordinated multiple accounts amplifying the same message or voting behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strawman sockpuppet (false flag) (type)
rubrics_metrics.description: A strawman sockpuppet (sometimes abbreviated strawpuppet) is a false flag pseudonym created to make a particular point of view look foolish or unwholesome in order to generate negative sentiment against it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These accounts typically behave in an unintelligent, uninformed, or bigoted manner (advancing 'straw man' arguments) so their puppeteers can easily refute them. The related 'concern troll' pretends to share a group's goals while sowing fear, uncertainty and doubt (FUD).

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigation and detection techniques
rubrics_metrics.description: A number of techniques have been developed to determine whether accounts are sockpuppets, including comparing the IP addresses of suspected sockpuppets, comparative analysis of the writing style of suspected sockpuppets, and temporal-based correlation (closely linked in time).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical detection combines multiple signals: IP/GeoIP lookup, stylometric analysis, posting timestamps/patterns, and cross-account behavioral correlation. The page cites GeoIP and writing-style comparisons as common investigative tools.

rubrics_metrics.name: GeoIP and IP address correlation
rubrics_metrics.description: Using GeoIP it is possible to look up the IP addresses and locate them; comparing IP addresses of suspected sockpuppets is a technique for investigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IP correlation is a strong technical signal but must be interpreted cautiously (shared networks, VPNs, proxies). Combine with other evidence such as timing and style.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing-style (stylometric) analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Comparative analysis of the writing style of suspected sockpuppets is used to identify linked accounts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stylometry can indicate common authorship but is probabilistic; use alongside metadata (timing, IPs, interaction patterns) and manual review to avoid false positives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporal correlation as an indicator
rubrics_metrics.description: Temporal-based correlation (closely linked in time) of activity between accounts is a detection technique.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Synchronized posting, rapid alternation between accounts, or concentrated bursts across multiple accounts strengthens a sockpuppet hypothesis when combined with other signals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community norms and platform policy response
rubrics_metrics.description: Sock puppets are unwelcome in many online communities and forums; Wikipedia and other platforms have policies (e.g., Wikimedia Foundation condemned paid advocacy sockpuppeting and banned Wiki-PR editing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating accounts, consider platform-specific rules (e.g., bans on undisclosed paid advocacy). Policy actions can include suspension, banning, cease-and-desist letters, and public condemnation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal risk under the Computer Fraud and Abuse Act (CFAA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Misrepresenting oneself online has been prosecuted under the CFAA (e.g., United States v. Drew), which prohibits 'accessing a computer without authorization via interstate commerce', though outcomes have varied and charges have been contested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legal exposure for creating fake accounts depends on jurisdiction, facts (e.g., terms-of-service violation, jurisdiction of servers), and case law; prosecutors have sometimes used CFAA charges but convictions and sentencing have varied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criminal charges: identity theft, criminal impersonation, aggravated harassment
rubrics_metrics.description: Using multiple sockpuppet accounts to attack and impersonate others has resulted in criminal convictions for identity theft, criminal impersonation, and aggravated harassment (e.g., People v. Golb).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serious abusive conduct using sockpuppets (impersonation, harassment) can be charged under ordinary criminal statutes; assess conduct against local criminal laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Civil liability: tortious interference and injunctive relief
rubrics_metrics.description: A court held that sock puppetry can be tortious interference with business relations and awarded injunctive relief, finding 'the act of falsifying multiple identities' wrongful because it creates a false impression that interferes with plaintiffs' business (New Directions for Young Adults, Inc. v. Davis).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Civil remedies can include removal of postings that create a false impression of multiple people; courts may nonetheless protect some speech (e.g., posts under true names) under the First Amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contexts and examples of harmful uses
rubrics_metrics.description: Documented examples include business promotion (company executives posting praise of their own companies), fake book and film reviews (authors praising their own books), blog commentary (writers posting under false names to defend themselves), and review-bombing on aggregator sites.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing suspicious accounts, compare against these known patterns: promotional praise, attack campaigns against critics or competitors, coordinated positive reviews, and concealed relationships to promoted entities.

rubrics_metrics.name: State-sponsored or government-directed sockpuppetry
rubrics_metrics.description: State-sponsored internet sockpuppetry is used for propaganda and influence operations (examples: U.S. contract to create fake personas for Operation Earnest Voice; Internet Research Agency activities linked to elections).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Large-scale, language-diverse, and highly coordinated networks (including use of contractor firms) suggest state or organizational campaigns rather than individual deception; flag for escalation to platform security or national-security researchers.
